text.p: The Signals and Syscalls Explorer can help you make sense of how processes interact with the kernel or other processes. In particular, it can help you keep track of file descriptors and what they are referring to.
Note: At this time, this tool requires raw events to enabled in settings.
On the left side of this tool you will find a tree of processes followed by a list of filesystem entries. Selecting an entry in this tree will update the syscalls and signals lists to the right.

The Processes and Threads will list all found processes directly under it. Selecting a process at this level will show signals for this process and syscalls for this process including all threads within the process, but excluding calls from any child processes. Expanding a process node will expose a list of threads within that process. Selecting a thread will limit the syscalls view to calls generated by that thread.

If a process spawns any children, there will be a node called Child Processes under the process threads. Selecting this node will show syscalls for the process itself, as well as any child processes and threads, including grand children. Selecting a child process will show syscalls for the process tree starting on that node. If you are interested in a particular child only, or a specific thread of a child, you need to find and select that child in the topmost process list.
Note: All known processes will be present in the topmost process list, even if they are also present as a child to another process.

The File System node contains a structured list of accessed file system entries. Clicking on an entry in this tree will list syscalls referencing the entry, including calls referencing the entry through a file descriptor.
Note: Some syscalls may reference a file or entry through a relative path. Since the absolute path is often unknown (not contained in the trace), these will show up under a dot (.) node.

Note: The list of accessed files and entries, or the list of accesses to a file or entry, may be incomplete due to limitations of mapping file descriptors to entries. For example, if a process opens a file for writing before tracing is started and writes to that file descriptor while tracing is enabled, $PNAME will not be able to tie those write calls to the file system entry.

The Syscalls tab contains a list of syscalls issued by the selected process, process tree or thread, or syscalls referencing the selected file system entry. Selecting an entry will show details to the right. Double clicking an entry will focus details views (such as the main trace view) on the entry of the call (or exit if the entry is unavailable). Failing calls will show up as red in the list.

The details will contain timestamps, what actor (thread) issued the call and any call data recorded by the tracer. If references to one or more file descriptors were identified, a File Descriptors node will be added containing a list of the identified file descriptors. For each file descriptor, a subtree with all knowledge $PNAME has about the descriptor will be added. Examples of information can include file name or in the case of a pipe what other file descriptor it is connected to.
The signals tab contain a list of signals generated by or for the selected process, as well as signals delivered to the selected process.
